sources.text: 4CEGC3011 – Machine Learning and its Applications Practice Questions: Modules 1 & 2 CMR University School of Engineering and Technology Department of Computer Engineering and Computer Science and Technology Practice Questions for MLA – Module 1 and 2 4CEGC3011: Machine Learning and its Applications | Semester V | AY 2026–27 Instructors: Dr. Pandava Sudharshan Babu, Dr. Jayashree S Module 1: Data, Datasets and Evaluation Metrics 1. Define Machine Learning. Differentiate between traditional programming and Machine Learn- ing with a suitable example. [5 Marks] 2. With a neat diagram, explain the relationship between Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Deep Learning. Give one real-world application of each. [5 Marks] 3. Explain the different types of data used in Machine Learning (numerical, categorical, text, image, audio, video) and state how each is converted into a numerical form before it reaches an ML model. [10 Marks] 4. Distinguish between features and labels with an example dataset. Explain the structure of a typical dataset in terms of rows, columns, instances and attributes. [5 Marks] 5. Explain the complete Machine Learning workflow from problem definition to model deployment with a neat block diagram. [10 Marks] 6. What are missing values? Explain any four techniques for handling missing values in a dataset, stating one advantage and one limitation of each. [10 Marks] 7. Explain Label Encoding and One-Hot Encoding with an example. State one situation where One-Hot Encoding is preferred over Label Encoding, and explain the dummy variable trap. [10 Marks] 8. A retail analytics team has collected the customer dataset given below. The two features are on very different scales, which biases distance-based models. Customer Age (years) Annual Income (Rs. ’000) C1 22 180 C2 35 420 C3 48 650 C4 29 300 C5 56 900 C6 41 540 Apply Min–Max Normalization to scale both features to the range [0, 1]. Show the formula, all intermediate values and the final normalized table (round to 3 decimals). Also rescale the Age column to the range [−1, 1] and state one limitation of Min–Max normalization. [10 Marks] 9. The following dataset records the temperature and humidity observed on five days. Apply Min–Max Normalization to scale both features to [0, 1]. Show all steps and the final normalized table. 1

8. Role of Individuals in Conservation of Natural Resources Water: Turn off taps, repair leaks, use rainwater harvesting and avoid wastage. Energy: Switch off appliances, use energy-efficient devices and prefer renewable energy where possible. Forests: Plant and protect trees and reduce unnecessary paper use. 3Rs: Reduce unnecessary consumption, reuse products and recycle paper, plastic, glass and metals. Fuel: Use public transport, walk or cycle for short distances and carpool. Waste: Segregate wet and dry waste, avoid single-use plastics and compost biodegradable waste. Conclusion: Individual actions, when adopted widely, can significantly reduce resource depletion and environmental pollution. 9. Natural Resources (NR) and Their Types Definition: Natural resources are materials and components obtained from nature that are useful to humans and other living organisms. Renewable resources: Resources that can naturally replenish themselves within a reasonable period. Examples: solar energy, wind energy, water, forests and biomass. Renewable resources are not unlimited. Non-renewable resources: Resources available in limited quantities that take a very long time to form. Examples: coal, petroleum, natural gas and minerals. Biotic resources: Obtained from living organisms, such as forests, animals and fish. Abiotic resources: Obtained from non-living components, such as water, air, minerals and sunlight. 10. Biodiversity – Definition and Types Definition: Biodiversity means the variety and variability of living organisms and ecosystems found in a particular area or on Earth. 1. Genetic diversity: Variation in genetic characteristics among individuals of the same species. Example: different varieties of rice or mango. 2. Species diversity: Variety of different species present in a particular area, such as different trees, birds, insects and mammals in a forest. 3. Ecosystem diversity: Variety of ecosystems in a region, such as forests, grasslands, deserts, rivers, wetlands and oceans. Importance: Maintains ecological balance, provides food and medicines, supplies raw materials, supports agriculture, provides ecosystem services and helps ecosystems adapt to environmental changes. Threats: Deforestation, habitat destruction, pollution, climate change, overexploitation and invasive species. Conservation: In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, while ex-situ conservation protects them outside their natural habitats, such as in zoos, botanical gardens and seed banks. Most Important for Exam

Prepare these first: Types of Ecosystem; Global Warming and its Effects; Greenhouse Effect; Climate Change; Ozone Layer and Ozone Depletion; Role of Individuals in Conservation of Natural Resources; Natural Resources and their Types; Biodiversity – Definition and Types; Consumers and Decomposers; Behavioural Changes. Exam strategy: If only two questions are expected, prepare Global Warming/Greenhouse Effect and Natural Resources/Biodiversity particularly well, including definitions, causes/types, effects, control or conservation measures and examples.

A fitness application stores the user records shown below. The features are measured in different units and must be brought onto a common scale before clustering. User Weight (kg) Daily Steps U1 52 3000 U2 68 7500 U3 75 12000 U4 60 5400 U5 90 15000 U6 81 9800 Apply Min–Max Normalization to bring both features into [0, 1]. Show the computation for each record and present the final normalized table (round to 3 decimals). If a new user records 20,000 steps, explain what happens to the previously computed normalized values. [10 Marks] 11. The marks obtained by six students in an aptitude test are recorded below. Before applying a distance-based classifier, the instructor wants every feature to have zero mean and unit variance. Student Score Practice Hours S1 40 2 S2 55 4 S3 60 5 S4 75 8 S5 85 9 S6 65 6 Perform Z-Score Standardization on both columns (use population standard deviation). Show the mean, standard deviation and the standardized table (round to 3 decimals). Identify which student is farthest from the mean in Score, and state when standardization is preferred over normalization. [10 Marks] 12. A bank records the details of six loan applicants as shown. Transform the features so that each has a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1. Applicant Credit Score Loan Amount (Rs. lakhs) A1 600 5 A2 720 12 A3 680 9 A4 750 15 A5 640 7 A6 700 10 Show the mean, standard deviation and the final standardized table (round to 3 decimals). Interpret the meaning of a negative z-score and explain how standardization handles outliers compared with Min–Max normalization. [10 Marks] 2
